speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you present with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my investigation, can you describe exactly how your balance and coordination have changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; the "drunk" appearance suggests significant incoordination. You mentioned the right side is worse—has this problem been steadily getting worse, or did it come on suddenly after a specific event like a fall?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

This diagnosis is highly probable given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, a known risk factor for PML, which presents with subacute gait and limb ataxia. I need to confirm the onset timeline and perform an urgent neurological exam to assess for other focal deficits.
